ai.description: *Minervarya goemchi* is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a brown dorsum featuring distinct longitudinal skin folds. It is identified by a prominent white mid-dorsal stripe and a dark, V-shaped interorbital bar.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya goemchi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent glandular fold along the dorsolateral region, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya goemchi* inhabits the Western Ghats of India, typically found in moist deciduous forests and along the edges of paddy fields at mid-to-high altitudes.
ai.behavior: *Minervarya goemchi* is primarily nocturnal, remaining active during the monsoon season when it emerges to forage for small invertebrates in moist, grassy habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya goemchi* breeds during the monsoon season (June–August). They are oviparous, laying clutches of approximately 200–300 eggs in temporary rain-fed pools.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya goemchi* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the state of Goa at elevations ranging from 50 to 800 meters above sea level.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Minervarya goemchi* consists of a series of rapid, pulsed chirps with a high pitch, typically heard in wet paddy fields and marshy habitats.
